newsitem.title: UK: EMU deal a plus for European debt but mark fragile.
newsitem.headline: EMU deal a plus for European debt but mark fragile.

text.p: Modest gains were on the cards for European bond markets after an agreement on single currency stability pact on Monday, analysts said, but the mark slipped on fears of a weaker euro.

European Union (EU) finance ministers meeting in Amsterdam under intense pressure to hammer out a deal, said they agreed to keep the budget stability pact intact while adding a separate resolution on jobs and growth to accomodate French demands.
"It looks like the EMU train chugs along -- what can derail it now?" said Brian Venables, senior bond analyst at ABM AMRO Haore Govett in Amsterdam.

"It looks like we're going for a broad EMU with as many countries as possible and to go ahead on time. This brings convergence back on the agenda...for Italy and Spain and Portugal to a degree," said Venables.
But such prospects troubled the mark as investors speculated on a looser interpretation of the European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) with peripherals also squeezing through the euro door.

"Given that it is a fudged compromise, it is not great for European currencies against the dollar, and not good for core European assets relative to those in the U.S.," said Rob Hayward, economic adviser at BankAmerica.
The mark dipped to the day's lows on European crosses. At 1345 GMT, it was quoted at 3.3730 to the French franc from 3.3738 in late European trade on Friday.
But it gained some lost ground against the dollar, trading at 1.7306 from 1.7342 earlier and from a low of 1.7407 on Friday.
